{{recipe}}

This '''carrot almond cake''' is kosher for Passover since it uses [[Cookbook:Matzo Meal|matzo meal]] instead of [[Cookbook:Wheat|wheat]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]].

==Ingredients==
* Matzo cake meal (for pan)
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], separated and at room temperature
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] light [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1½ cup finely [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] (optional)
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ cup white [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 1 cup toasted [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]], finely grated
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] fine-ground [[Cookbook:Matzo Meal|matzo meal]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] 

==Procedure==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F.
# Grease the bottom of an 8-inch [[Cookbook:Springform Pan|springform pan]], and lightly dust with almond meal.
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] egg yolks and brown sugar in a large bowl with an electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] until thick and light (about 5 minutes). A slowly-dissolving ribbon should form when the beaters are lifted. 
# Stir in carrots and vanilla.
# Clean and dry the beater. Whip the egg whites with the salt until soft peaks form.
# Gradually add the granulated sugar and beat until the egg whites make firm peaks.
# Gently [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] the whites into the egg yolk mixture.
# Combine the almonds, matzo meal, and cinnamon. Fold gently into the egg mixture.
# Turn the batter into prepared pan, smoothing the top.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] until tester comes out clean (about 1 hour).
# Immediately run a knife around the edges, then leave to cool in the pan on a rack.
# Remove from the springform pan.
